The scenarios are fairly straightforward and explain what the Fed is looking for. We can all watch the economic data—CPI, PPI, and import prices for June—this week and continue to update the likely path for the federal funds rate. The data-driven Fed is alive and well.
The two scenarios in the minutes also help us interpret the dot plot. Fed officials were divided in their outlook for inflation, not in how to react to inflation.

What will it take for the Fed to hike?

The June minutes laid out two scenarios, and the committee is split right down the middle. Fed officials were divided in their outlook for inflation, not in how to react to it. 

More in my new Substack post: stayathomemacro.substack.com/p/what-will-...
It's a reallocation of resources, but the resources are there.

My two cents on the Warsh task forces: Warsh is an ideas person, not a details person. The Fed is a detail-oriented place, and task forces will provide him with some detailed proposals. Then the actual debate on the committee begins.
No one with a background in national accounts or measurement is a big blind spot, but it fits the pattern of the other task forces: supply details for the ideas Warsh voiced.
